added_models.model: Mouse allergic airways disease after Fel d 1 peptide immunotherapy (dual OVA/Fel d 1 sensitisation)

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level only (JACI paywalled; Europe PMC and fc.py returned no full text). Which Fel d 1 peptides were dosed (the Cat-PAD mix or the lab's own) and the mouse strain are not in the abstract; no earlier conference abstract found (CSACI 2015/2016 and AllerGen 2016 proceedings searched).
efficacy.note: Larché-lab mouse model: Fel d 1 peptide treatment protected dually sensitised mice from airway eosinophilia and TH2 infiltration on cat allergen challenge.
efficacy.short: Mouse Fel d 1 peptide model published
efficacy.quote: Functional tolerance to each allergen was assessed in a model of allergic airways disease in which treated mice were protected from eosinophilia, goblet cell hyperplasia, and TH2 cell infiltration.
efficacy.judgement: The only animal model found for any member drug: Europe PMC sweeps on Cat-PAD, ToleroMune, SPIRE, Fel d 1 peptides, hdmASIT+, SQ tree tablet and cat SLIT with mouse/murine/humanized/transgenic terms return nothing else. First use dated to the online publication (2018-06-12).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: mouse: protection from eosinophilia, goblet cell hyperplasia and TH2 infiltration on cat allergen challenge; field Phase 3 Combined Score 1.04 and 1.00 vs 1.05 placebo (SE 0.068), n 467/470/470
efficacy.confidence_note: Paired by us: model side is the abstract only (JACI paywalled), patient side is the posted registry results. The model paper went online 2018-06-12, two years after the Phase 3 top-line failure (2016-06-20); whether the mouse work was run before or after that readout is not stated, so this may be a failed retrodiction, which is also contra (decision 10).

patient_trials.quote: Mean Combined Score in Cat-PAD Treatment Groups Compared With Placebo

efficacy.note: Mouse model showed peptide-induced protection; the 1,408-patient field Phase 3 found Combined Score 1.04/1.00 vs 1.05 placebo, no treatment effect.
efficacy.short: Mouse protection, field loss to placebo
efficacy.quote: Mean Combined Score in Cat-PAD Treatment Groups Compared With Placebo: Cat-PAD Treatment 1 (1 Course) 1.04; Cat-PAD Treatment 2 (2 Courses) 1.00; Placebo 1.05
efficacy.judgement: Model predicts the class works (airway protection after peptide treatment); the field primary showed none. Year is the first date both sides were public (model epub 2018-06). The mouse endpoint is airway inflammation, the human one rhinoconjunctivitis symptoms plus medication, so direction only. product_in_model left null because the abstract does not say the peptides were the Cat-PAD mix.

added_models.model: Patient PBMC Fel d 1-specific CD4+ T cells (ex vivo), Cat-PAD

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (PMID 21211644; JACI Jan 2011). The PBMC proliferation/cytokine assays picked the Cat-PAD peptides and ran alongside CP001 (NCT00685711, first posted 2008-05-28), so first use could be 2008 by proxy.
engagement.note: Cat-allergic PBMC proliferation and IFN-γ/IL-10/IL-13 responses picked the immunodominant Fel d 1 peptides that became Cat-PAD; no dosed-patient T-cell readout yet.
engagement.short: PBMC T-cell assay picked Cat-PAD peptides
engagement.quote: Immunodominant sequences were identified on the basis of proliferative and cytokine (IFN-γ, IL-10, and IL-13) responses.
engagement.judgement: A different ex-vivo system from the draft's basophil histamine-release track (different cells, different prediction: T-cell engagement rather than IgE cross-linking), so its own track. Opener dated to publication as the basophil track is.

engagement.magnitude_basis: CRTh2 surface expression on Fel d 1 tetramer+ CD4+ T cells, placebo vs active P = 0.047; frequency, the other four chemokine receptors and memory phenotype unchanged
engagement.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC6817377). Samples from NCT00867906 (Cat-PAD safety study in cat-allergic subjects with controlled asthma, first posted 2009-03-24, n 48 estimated, no results posted). One receptor of five moved at P = 0.047; the authors conclude Cat-PAD 'may decrease' CRTh2.
engagement.note: In Cat-PAD-dosed patients Fel d 1-specific CD4+ T cells kept their frequency and phenotype; only CRTh2 fell (P=0.047), a partial move.
engagement.short: Only CRTh2 moved on target T cells
engagement.quote: However, a significant reduction in cell surface expression of CRTh2 was observed between the placebo and active groups (P = 0.047).
engagement.judgement: Scored same with source_calls_it partial (status table: partial agreement). The 2011 assay read proliferation and cytokines; Rudulier read tetramer frequency and chemokine receptors on the same cells, so the match is on the system, not the identical readout. Readout is direct: the peptides' target cells examined ex vivo. A contra reading (the stated hypothesis of an altered chemokine-receptor profile mostly failed) is defensible; hence low confidence.

added_models.model: Birch-homologous-group cross-reactivity ex vivo (patient sera IgE/IgG4/IgE-blocking factor, passive-sensitisation BAT, T-cell lines), SQ tree SLIT-tablet

efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7984359). Opener for a system first reported after the Phase 3 (EudraCT 2015-004821-15; no ClinicalTrials.gov record, so registry_date is null).
efficacy.note: ALK's ex-vivo cross-reactivity panel: Phase 3 sera (IgE, IgG4, IgE-blocking factor, BAT) and T-cell lines across alder, hazel, hornbeam, beech, chestnut.
efficacy.quote: T-cell responses (proliferation) to allergen extracts and peptide pools (group 1 allergens) were investigated in T-cell lines from 29 untreated birch pollen-allergic individuals.
efficacy.judgement: First use is the publication (epub 2020-12-08); samples were drawn during the Phase 3 but the cross-reactivity analyses were reported only after the alder/hazel-season result was known. A different system from the chamber track (ex-vivo serology and T-cell lines, predicting cross-protection rather than dose).

efficacy.magnitude_basis: serum IgE birch vs alder/hazel/hornbeam r ≥ .93, treatment-induced IgG4 r ≥ .85, BAT EC50 raised for birch, alder and hornbeam; Phase 3 TCS reduced in the alder/hazel and birch seasons
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read (PMC7984359); the comparison is to the Phase 3 tree-pollen-season (alder/hazel) key secondary, not the birch-season primary, so endpoint_role is null. Phase 3 has only a EudraCT number (2015-004821-15).

patient_trials.quote: The trial demonstrated the efficacy and safety of the SQ tree SLIT-tablet compared with placebo during the BPS and TPS in adolescents and adults with birch pollen-induced ARC (EudraCT 2015-004821-15).

efficacy.note: After the Phase 3 showed alder/hazel-season efficacy, the ex-vivo panel reproduced it: IgE, IgG4, blocking and T-cell responses cross-react across the homologous group.
efficacy.quote: Systematic analyses of T-cell and antibody cross-reactivities before and during birch pollen extract AIT provide the immunological basis for the observed clinical effect of SQ tree SLIT-tablet treatment
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the source itself frames its analyses as the basis for the observed clinical cross-protection, so retro, never same. Scored on the tree-pollen-season effect, a key secondary. The IgE cross-reactivity idea behind the homologous-group definition predates the product, but no member-specific prospective ex-vivo paper was found, so no prospective credit.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: T-cell-line responses to Bet v 1 peptides correlate with the corresponding Aln g 1, Cor a 1 and a subset of Que a 1 peptides, confirmed by pMHCII tetramers; clinical effect reported in alder/hazel, birch and oak seasons
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Front Immunol, OA, PMC10702988); the same 29 untreated T-cell lines as Würtzen 2021, extended to oak peptides and tetramers. The tablet is not in this T-cell-line arm (product_in_model false). Strengthens, no status change.
efficacy.note: Same T-cell lines re-read with Bet v 1-homologous peptides and tetramers: cross-reactivity extends to oak, matching the oak-season effect.
efficacy.quote: T cells from birch tree pollen allergic individuals respond to multiple trees within the birch homologous group in accordance with the level of sequence homology between Bet v 1 family members
efficacy.judgement: Second retrodiction on the same track, flagged strengthens; it adds oak (the EEC and post hoc oak-season effect) and tetramer confirmation but changes nothing.

considered_not_added: Mouse Der p 1 peptide allergic-airways model (Moldaver 2014, Mucosal Immunol): Der p 1 peptides are not a member drug and no member patient comparison exists; hdmASIT+ is a different HDM product.
Fel d 1 peptide-PreS fusion, Fel d 1 bioparticle, Fel d 1 hypoallergen mouse models (Niespodziana 2011, Curin 2014, 2026 Allergy): non-member products; no comparison with a member drug.

Human peptide-challenge and linked-epitope-suppression studies (Campbell 2009 JEM; Haselden/Larché 2005-2007): earlier 12-peptide Fel d 1 mix, not Cat-PAD, and human mechanistic studies rather than a model with a patient comparison.
HLA-DR binding assay for Fel d 1 peptides (Worm 2011): a biochemical selection step, no prediction compared with patients.
ToleroMune Ragweed chamber trials NCT01198613 / NCT02061709 and field observational NCT01398137: existing chamber track (checker's missing list), not a new system.
Cat-PAD paediatric safety NCT01921257, Phase 3 follow-on NCT02040844, tree-tablet paediatric NCT04878354: patient-side records for existing tracks, left to the adjudicator.
hdmASIT+ and ALK cat SLIT-tablet: no animal, humanized, ex-vivo T-cell or basophil-activation paper found for either member.
In-silico / QSP dose models and human genetic models: none found for any member.

ITULAZAX homologous-group indication (EU DCP 2019): regulator acceptance rests on the Phase 3 alder/hazel-season data plus cross-reactivity, not on model data in lieu of a trial; not a model system, regulatory_reliance left false.
